page: UpCloud GPU-8xCPU-64GB-1xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server configured with an AMD EPYC 9575F processor featuring 8 vCPUs across 8 physical cores on the x86_64 architecture. The system includes 64 GB of system memory, providing 8 GB per core, and is equipped with a single NVIDIA L40S GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture with 48 GB of VRAM. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, and virtualization is managed via KVM.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 10%. Multi-core performance for stress-ng and Geekbench falls in the average range. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks register average speeds, while Passmark memory scores are strong. For LLM inference, the server demonstrates strong to top-tier performance on small and medium models, but exhibits a tradeoff with weak prompt processing performance on large 70B models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server pairs a high-end NVIDIA L40S GPU with a shared AMD EPYC CPU allocation, offering a dense GPU-to-CPU resource ratio. This configuration is suitable for workloads such as machine learning inference, medium-scale LLM execution, image processing, and text processing. However, the lack of local storage requires external storage attachments, and the shared CPU allocation may introduce variability for sustained multi-core compute-bound tasks.
